title: urn:qauth:ia:upstream_link:v1-rc.0
description: Shown once an upstream identity provider proved an identity no account of the realm holds (#670; ADR-020 §3). The person picks a new account with that identity, which is offered only where the realm allows sign-up and the new account can be verified (`create`), or the account they already have, which they then sign in to in this interaction under its MFA policy: the `identifier` step, and every step that account’s sign-in asks for. That sign-in offers the realm’s other upstream providers beside its first step, never the one being linked (#1080): one proves the account only through an identity the account already holds, a passkey the account holds is still asked for after it, and an identity no account holds signs in to nothing and creates nothing. No password reset is offered. The identity joins that account only once that sign-in completes, in the same browser and the same interaction. Nothing on the step names the identity or the account: no address and no hint, and no account is ever found by an attribute such as an email address. Works without JavaScript: each choice is a button of a plain form post.

name.description: The provider’s name as the operator set it, for the screen’s text.

create.description: Whether the person may start a new account with the identity: the realm allows sign-up, the new account can be verified (the provider vouches for its address, or gave one an emailed code verifies), and the provider’s claims fit what the interaction keeps. `false` offers the existing account only.

decision.description: A new account with the identity, or the existing account the person signs in to next.

amr.description: The RFC 8176 `amr` values a successful answer adds to the transaction: none, because the step proves no authenticator.
